absent: Locking, concurrency, reference counting and lifetime rules for links, ports, tunnels and statistics are not shown.
Function entry points, system call numbers, ioctl commands, netlink message types and error returns are not shown.
State transition rules for spanning tree, bond aggregation, VXLAN learning, neighbor discovery and netkit verdict processing are not shown.
Packet format details beyond the Ethernet header and port ranges, including payload handling, checksums, encryption and segmentation behavior, are not shown.
Timing, timer expiry, default intervals, sysctl ranges and validation limits for the enumerated attributes are not shown.
Memory allocation, queueing, driver binding and hardware offload mechanics behind the attributes are not shown.

findings.text: These headers expose stable user space networking ABI for Ethernet framing, link statistics and link netlink attributes. Consumers may rely on the Ethernet header layout, the counter structures and the attribute identifier sets for configuring and observing links, bridges, VLANs and tunnels.

Low Ethernet protocol identifiers use small integer values starting at one for 802.3 framing, two for AX25, three for all packets, four for 802.2, five for internal SNAP, six for DDCMP, seven for wide area PPP, eight for PPP multilink and nine for LocalTalk. Values distinguish dummy or internal framing from real wire types.

Middle protocol identifiers continue with twelve for CAN, thirteen for CAN with flexible rate, fourteen for CAN with extended length, sixteen for AppleTalk over PPP, seventeen for token ring 802.2, twenty one for Mobitex, twenty two for card control, twenty three for infrared, twenty four for Econet, twenty five for HDLC, twenty six for ArcNet, twenty seven for distributed switch tagging and twenty eight for trailer tagging.

Upper multiplex identifiers use values around two hundred forty five to two hundred fifty four. They cover Phonet, low rate personal area frames, CAIF, multiplexed distributed switch, Qualcomm aggregation, management component transport and GRE OSI. The GRE OSI value is documented as appearing on the wire, not internal only, unlike several low dummy values.

Ethernet header holds a destination hardware address array followed by a source hardware address array, each sized by the Ethernet address length, followed by a sixteen bit big endian protocol field. The layout is packed with no padding so wire order matches memory order.

Two guard macros mark user space visibility and single inclusion. One enables the Ethernet header definition for user space, the other prevents repeated inclusion of the link netlink header. Presence of the guard indicates stable user ABI rather than kernel internal only content.

Thirty two bit link statistics hold about two dozen unsigned counters in fixed order. The general group tracks packets, bytes, errors and drops in both directions plus multicast and collisions. Receive detail tracks length, overrun, cyclic, framing, fifo and missed errors. Transmit detail tracks aborted, carrier, fifo, heartbeat and window errors. The tail tracks compressed packet pair and a no handler counter.

Sixty four bit link statistics mirror the thirty two bit counter themes with wider unsigned counters in the same conceptual order. General, receive detail, transmit detail, compression and no handler groups correspond, with one additional trailing counter for packets dropped as belonging to another host.

Hardware statistics provide a compact nine counter subset with sixty four bit width. They track packets, bytes, errors and drops in both directions plus multicast, without the detailed error breakdown or compression and handler fields found in the fuller structures.

Interface mapping describes legacy device resources in order. It starts with two sixty four bit memory bounds and a sixty four bit base address, then a sixteen bit interrupt line, an eight bit direct memory access channel and an eight bit port identifier.

Top level link netlink attributes form a zero based enumeration beginning with an unspecified sentinel. Entries identify link naming, addressing, mtu, peer linkage, queueing, statistics, cost, priority, master, wireless events, protocol info, queue length, mapping, weight, operational state, link mode, nested link info, namespaces, aliases, virtual functions, extended statistics, ports, address family detail, grouping, masks, promiscuity, queue counts, carrier state and change counts, physical port and switch identity, namespace identifiers, protocol down state with reasons, segmentation limits, padding, packet steering, events, mtu bounds, properties, alternative names, permanent address, parent device names, pacing, immutability, headroom and tailroom. A separate small enumeration carries protocol down reason mask and value. Public max is defined as one less than the internal sentinel.

Every attribute and mode enumeration in this family follows the same bound rule. An internal double underscore max sentinel closes the list and the public max equals that sentinel minus one. Code iterating or validating attributes must treat the public max as inclusive and the internal sentinel as exclusive.

Link attributes follow the interface info message in a netlink payload. The attribute start is found after the aligned size of that fixed header, and the remaining payload length is the netlink payload after the same header. Receivers must use alignment aware sizing, not plain structure size.

Internet version four link attributes carry configuration under a small enumeration with unspecified base and public max rule. Version six attributes cover flags, configuration, statistics, multicast data, cache timing, ICMPv6 statistics, device token, address generation mode and router advertisement mtu. Generation modes use zero for EUI64, one for none, two for stable privacy and three for random. Both families reserve zero for unspecified.

Bridge master attributes enumerate timers, aging, spanning tree state, priority, VLAN filtering and protocol, forwarding masks, root and bridge identity, path cost, topology change flags and timers, garbage collection timing, group address, forwarding database flush, multicast routing and snooping controls, query intervals and counts, hash tuning, netfilter hooks, default port VLAN, padding, per port statistics toggles, IGMP and MLD versions, boolean options, querier state, learned entry counts and spanning tree mode. Zero is unspecified and public max follows the minus one rule.

Spanning tree control modes use zero for automatic, one for user space control and two for kernel control. An internal sentinel follows and the public max is one less, so only the three named values are valid.
Bridge identifier layout holds a two byte priority field followed by a six byte address matching Ethernet length. Total size is eight bytes with priority first on the wire.
Bridge port forwarding modes reserve zero for unspecified and use one for hairpin forwarding. No other values are defined in this fragment.

Bridge port attributes enumerate spanning tree state, priority, cost, forwarding mode, guard and protection flags, fast leave, learning controls, flood controls for unicast, multicast, broadcast and unknown, proxy ARP variants, designated root and bridge identity, designated port and cost, port identifier and number, topology acknowledgment, pending configuration, age and delay and hold timers, flush, multicast router state, padding, tunnel and forwarding mask controls, neighbor suppression variants, isolation, backup port and next hop, ring openness flags, host tracking limits and counts, locked and authentication flags and group counts and limits. Zero is unspecified with public max one less than internal sentinel.
Cache information holds four thirty two bit unsigned values in order. They convey maximum reassembly length, table update timestamp, reachable time and retransmit time for address handling.

Nested link information attributes distinguish kind strings, device data, extended statistics and slave kind with slave data. Zero is unspecified and public max follows the minus one rule, framing how virtual link types carry type specific blobs.

VLAN attributes cover identifier, flags, egress and ingress quality mapping, and protocol, with zero unspecified and public max minus one. A second small enumeration carries quality of service mappings with unspecified base and a single mapping entry type, also bounded by a minus one max.

VLAN flag state pairs a thirty two bit flag word with a thirty two bit mask word. Quality mapping pairs a thirty two bit source priority with a thirty two bit destination priority. Both structures use fixed order with the selector first.

MACVLAN attributes cover operation mode, flags, address mode and address list handling with counts, plus broadcast queue length, use and cutoff. Modes are sparse powers of two with one for private, two for VEPA, four for bridge, eight for passthrough and sixteen for source based. Address operations are ordered add, delete, flush then set. Two single bit flags control promiscuity suppression and destination skipping.

Virtual routing and forwarding attributes are minimal. Master and port each carry a table identifier under a tiny enumeration with unspecified zero and public max minus one, separating master table selection from port table binding.

MACsec attributes enumerate secure channel identifier, port, integrity length, cipher suite, replay window, encoding association, encryption and protection toggles, identifier inclusion, end station and confidentiality flags, replay protection, validation mode, padding and offload selection. Zero is unspecified with public max minus one.

XFRM link attributes carry peer link index, interface identifier and metadata collection flag under a tiny enumeration. MACsec validation uses zero for disabled, one for check and two for strict. MACsec offload uses zero for off, one for physical layer and two for media access layer. Each enumeration closes with an internal end sentinel and a public max one less.

IPVLAN attributes carry mode and flags under a tiny enumeration. Modes use zero for layer two, one for layer three and two for layer three with segregation. Flags use low bits with one for private and two for VEPA behavior.

Tunnel control message layout starts with an eight bit family and an eight bit flag field, followed by sixteen reserved bits and a thirty two bit interface index. Flags qualify the request while family selects address handling.

Netkit verdicts are sparse with negative one for next, zero for pass, two for drop and seven for redirect. Device modes are layer two then layer three. Pairing distinguishes paired versus single device setup. Scrub levels are none then default. Link attributes for netkit cover peer info, primary selection, policies for both ends, mode, scrub for both ends, headroom, tailroom and pairing, with zero unspecified and public max minus one.
Tunnel message flags define a statistics request in the low bit. The valid user mask currently allows only that bit, so other flag bits must be zero from user space.

VXLAN filtering starts with per entry statistics counters for bytes, packets, drops and errors in both directions plus padding. Entries bind a start and end identifier with IPv4 or IPv6 group and attached statistics. A filter level nests entries. Main VXLAN attributes cover identifier, group and link, local addresses for both families, time to live and service type, learning, aging, limits, source port range, proxy, route short circuit, miss notifications, destination port, checksum controls, remote checksum offload, group policy, partial checksum handling, metadata collection, label, generic encapsulation, time to live inheritance, dont fragment handling, filter binding, local bypass, label policy, reserved bits and multicast routing. All use zero unspecified with minus one max.
VXLAN source port range holds low then high as sixteen bit big endian values. Order is fixed with low first.

VXLAN dont fragment policy uses zero for unset, one for set and two for inherit. Label policy uses zero for fixed and one for inherit. Each closes with an internal end sentinel and a public max one less.

GENEVE attributes cover identifier, remote addresses for both families, time to live and service type, destination port, metadata collection, checksum controls, label, time to live inheritance, dont fragment handling, inner protocol inheritance, port range, GRO hint and local addresses for both families. Dont fragment policy mirrors VXLAN with zero unset, one set and two inherit plus end sentinel and minus one max.
GENEVE port range holds low then high as sixteen bit big endian values with low first, matching the VXLAN range shape.

Bare UDP attributes cover destination port, ether type, minimum source port and multiprotocol mode. PPP attributes carry only a device file descriptor. GTP roles use zero for gateway node and one for serving node. GTP attributes carry two file descriptors, hash size, role, socket creation flag, restart count and local addresses for both families. All use zero unspecified with minus one max.

Bond master attributes cover mode, active slave, link monitoring timers and delays, carrier use, ARP interval and targets with validation, primary selection, failover MAC policy, transmit hash policy, IGMP resend, peer notification counts and delays, slave activity, minimum links, packet distribution, LACP rate and selection and activity, actor priority and keys and system identity, dynamic balancing, missed limits, IPv6 targets, coupled control, neighbor broadcast and strict LACP. Aggregator info carries aggregator identity, port count, actor and partner keys and partner address. Slave attributes carry state, media status, failure count, permanent address, queue identity, aggregator binding, actor and partner port states, priorities and churn states. All use zero unspecified with minus one max.

Capturing all packets is explicitly cautioned as heavy and overly broad. Treating GRE OSI as internal only risks wire incompatibility because it is defined as used on the wire. Assuming natural alignment for the packed Ethernet header risks faults on strict alignment targets because no padding is present.

Counter families preserve conceptual order across widths. The sixty four bit full statistics correspond entry wise to the thirty two bit set with wider storage, and the hardware subset corresponds to the leading general counters. Implementations must not reorder fields and must zero extend when converting from narrow to wide rather than reinterpret memory.
